explanation: Keep one current entry per sorted array in a min-heap and track their maximum. Record the range, then advance an array containing the minimum, since advancing any other array cannot reduce the current range. Stop when one array is exhausted.
timeComplexity: O(N log k), N total entries and k arrays. There is one maintained head per array and at most one advance per input entry.
spaceComplexity: O(k). The heap or ordered collection holds one head per input array.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The current selection contains one entry per array. If its minimum is retained, advancing any other selected entry cannot decrease the range, so an improved range must eventually advance an array attaining that minimum. The algorithm performs that necessary move each time and records every range before an array is exhausted.
walkthrough: For [[1,7],[3,6],[4,8]], begin with (1,3,4), range 3. Advancing minima reaches (7,6,4), range 3, then (7,6,8), range 2. No smaller range is found, so return 2. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: The input may contain more than three sorted arrays.
Equal selected values can give range zero.
